pests.economic_threshold_level: 8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive nights OR 10% damaged green bolls (rosette flowers observed)
pests.damage_symptoms: Larvae bore into squares, flowers, and bolls. Attacked flowers show 'rosette flower' symptom where petals twist together. Bolls show premature drop, fiber staining, and locule burrowing.
pests.natural_predators: Trichogramma bactrae, Bracon greeni, Chrysoperla zastrowi

pests.economic_threshold_level: 5-10 insects/hill at tillering; 15-20 insects/hill at panicle initiation
pests.damage_symptoms: Both nymphs and adults congregate at base of plant and suck sap. Infested plants turn yellow and dry up rapidly, resulting in circular patches of dried crop called 'hopper burn'.
pests.natural_predators: Mirid bug (Cyrtorhinus lividipennis), Wolf spider (Lycosa pseudoannulata)

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1-2 thrips per leaf or upward curling on 10% seedlings
pests.damage_symptoms: Lacerate leaf surface and suck exudate. Leaves curl upwards (boat-shaped). Stunted plant growth, bronzing of leaves, reduced flower bud formation.
pests.natural_predators: Anthocorid bugs (Orius tantillus), Green lacewing (Chrysoperla carnea)

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1 egg mass/sq.m or 5% dead hearts at vegetative stage; 1 moth/sq.m or 2% white ears at flowering
pests.damage_symptoms: Larvae bore into central shoot causing 'dead heart' at vegetative stage (easily pulled out) and empty, erect white chaffy panicles ('white earhead') at reproductive stage.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1-2 folded damaged leaves with larvae per hill
pests.damage_symptoms: Larva folds leaf blade longitudinally and scrapes green chlorophyll from inside, creating longitudinal transparent white streaks. Severe infestation gives field a scorched white look.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 6-8 adults or nymphs per leaf on upper/middle canopy
pests.damage_symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck phloem sap, secrete sticky honeydew promoting black sooty mold growth on leaves and lint. Acts as principal vector for Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV).
pests.natural_predators: Chrysoperla zastrowi, Coccinella septempunctata, Encarsia formosa

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1-2 nymphs per leaf or downward cupping of leaf margin (Grade II injury)
pests.damage_symptoms: Nymphs walk sideways on underside of leaves and suck sap while injecting toxic saliva. Leaf margins turn yellow, then bronze/brick red, curl downward ('hopper burn').

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1 larva per plant or 5% damaged squares/bolls
pests.damage_symptoms: Caterpillar feeds on squares and green bolls thrusting head inside while keeping rest of body outside. Clean circular boreholes surrounded by fecal pellets.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 2-3 mites per leaf on top canopy
pests.damage_symptoms: Mites suck sap from tender shoots. Leaves curl downwards (inverted boat shape / inverted cup), elongate into 'rat-tail' symptom with thickened dark green leathery texture.
pests.natural_predators: Phytoseiid predatory mites (Amblyseius swirskii, Neoseiulus longispinosus)

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1 egg mass or 1 skeletonized leaf patch per 10 plants
pests.damage_symptoms: Gregarious early instar caterpillars skeletonize leaves leaving parchment-like veins. Later instars voraciously defoliate plants, cut stems, and bore into chilli pods.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1 larva/plant or 5% fruit damage
pests.damage_symptoms: Larvae bore into green and ripening fruits making round holes, leading to entry of rot pathogens and fruit dropping.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1-2 active mines per leaf or 20-30 moths/pheromone trap/week
pests.damage_symptoms: Larvae feed as leaf miners creating large transparent blotches (mines) in leaf mesophyll. Also bore into growing buds, stems, and fruits leaving pinhole puncture marks.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 10-15 aphids per earhead / tiller at heading stage
pests.damage_symptoms: Colonies of aphids suck sap from leaves, flag leaf sheath, and developing earheads, resulting in chaffy ears, shriveled grains, and reduced test weight.
pests.natural_predators: Coccinella septempunctata, Syrphid fly larvae (Episyrphus balteatus)

pests.economic_threshold_level: Presence of fresh soil galleries and wilting seedlings in patches
pests.damage_symptoms: Termites feed on underground roots and stem base of germinating seedlings and mature plants, causing yellowing, drying, and lodging; affected tillers pull out easily.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 5% damaged plants with larvae at early whorl; 10% at mid-whorl stage
pests.damage_symptoms: Pinholes and large irregular papery windowpanes on whorl leaves. Deep feeding inside central whorl with excessive sawdust-like fecal frass accumulation. Destroys growing point ('dead heart').
pests.natural_predators: Earwig (Euborellia annulipes), Telenomus remus, Nomuraea rileyi
pests.citation: ICAR-IIMR & DPPQS Fall Armyworm National Campaign 2025

pests.economic_threshold_level: 10% plants showing pinholes or dead hearts
pests.damage_symptoms: Shot holes in leaf whorls; larvae bore into central shoots causing vegetative dead hearts. In later stages, tunnels through stalks causing stem breakage and lodging.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 5 active larvae per plant or 20% damaged leaves
pests.damage_symptoms: Larvae mine into tender leaflets creating blister-like mines. Later instars web leaflets together and feed within, giving the entire crop a scorched brownish appearance.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1-2 egg masses or 8 larvae per 10-meter row
pests.damage_symptoms: Gregarious caterpillars migrate en masse across fields completely devastating green vegetation down to ground level within hours.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1 grub per square meter in soil
pests.damage_symptoms: C-shaped fleshy white grubs chew taproots underground. Infested plants turn pale, wilt, and die in scattered patches; pull out effortlessly.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 5-10% plants showing girdled stems
pests.damage_symptoms: Female beetle makes two parallel ring cuts around petiole or stem and oviposits between them. Plant portion above ring withers and droops; larva tunnels downward inside pith.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 3-4 larvae per meter row length
pests.damage_symptoms: Larvae walk with looping motion and consume leaf lamina leaving only veins and midribs, leading to heavy defoliation during flowering and pod development.
pests.natural_predators: Trichogramma chilonis, Bacillus thuringiensis, Nomuraea rileyi

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1 larva per plant or 5% pod damage
pests.damage_symptoms: Larvae bore into developing pods, consume green seeds from inside, leaving large circular bore holes and dropping frass outside.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 5-10% infested green pods
pests.damage_symptoms: Maggots feed inside green seeds without external symptoms until adult fly cuts an exit hole window before emerging; damaged seeds lose germination and market value.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1 larva per meter row or 1 moth/pheromone trap/day
pests.damage_symptoms: Larva feeds on tender leaflets in vegetative stage, then defoliates flowers and bores into developing pods, eating developing seeds and reducing yield by up to 50%.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 20-25% plants infested or 1.5 - 2.0 cm aphid colony on central shoot tip
pests.damage_symptoms: Dense colonies of small greenish aphids suck sap from inflorescence, floral buds, and pods, curling flowers and resulting in pod shriveling and poor oil content.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1 larva per square meter or 2 larvae per plant at seedling stage
pests.damage_symptoms: Greenish-black cylindrical larvae feed on leaves from edges towards midrib making large irregular holes, causing complete defoliation of young seedlings.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 15% dead hearts during formative stage (up to 120 DAP)
pests.damage_symptoms: Larva enters below ground level and tunnels upward, destroying central spindle and producing foul-smelling 'dead heart' that pulls out easily.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 10% dead hearts or presence of red shot holes on leaf midribs
pests.damage_symptoms: Shot holes on leaves, red tunnel along leaf midrib, destruction of growing tip resulting in bunchy top appearance with profuse lateral sprouting.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 30 thrips per plant at vegetative / bulb initiation stage
pests.damage_symptoms: Adults and nymphs congregate in leaf sheath axils, rasp epidermal tissues creating silvery white blotches and streaks. Leaves distort, dry from tip down, reducing bulb size.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 5% leaf infestation in field or 2-4 moths/pheromone trap/week in store
pests.damage_symptoms: In field, larvae mine leaves and tunnel through petioles into exposed tubers. In country stores, caterpillars bore winding tunnels through tubers filled with dark silken frass.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 5% dead hearts or bore holes on pseudostems
pests.damage_symptoms: Larvae bore into pseudostems and feed internally, resulting in yellowing and drying of central shoot ('dead heart'). Frass extrudes from boreholes.

pests.economic_threshold_level: Presence of white circular scales on seed rhizomes before storage/planting
pests.damage_symptoms: Circular greyish-white scales encrust rhizomes in storage and field, sucking sap, leading to shriveling, desiccation, and complete loss of germination.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 5% silver shoots at tillering stage
pests.damage_symptoms: Maggot feeds at growing tip of apical meristem, transforming leaf sheath into a hollow, tubular silvery-white gall called 'silver shoot' or 'onion leaf', preventing panicle formation.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 1-2 bugs per hill or 5 bugs per sq. meter at milking stage
pests.damage_symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck milky sap from developing grains during early morning and evening hours. Grains become empty, spotted brown, or chaffy, giving off an unpleasant buggy smell.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 5 whiteflies per leaf or 5% webbed flowers/pods
pests.damage_symptoms: Whiteflies transmit Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus; Maruca larvae web flowers and pods together, feeding internally on seeds.

pests.economic_threshold_level: 20-25 nymphs/puparia per square inch on lower leaf surface
pests.damage_symptoms: Nymphs suck sap from underside of leaves; leaves turn yellow and pinkish-purple, coated with black sooty mold; sucrose recovery drops by 1-2 units.

diseases.symptoms: Spindle-shaped / diamond-shaped lesions on leaves with dark brown borders and grayish-white centers. Neck blast causes blackening of neck node, panicles break and hang down, producing empty chaffy grains.
diseases.favorable_weather: High relative humidity (>90%), night temperature 19-23°C, prolonged morning dew (4-6 hours), overcast skies.

diseases.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular spots on leaves delimited by veins. Lesions coalesce turning reddish-brown to black. Progresses along veins to petioles and stems causing 'black arm', and rotting of young bolls.
diseases.favorable_weather: Warm temperature (28-32°C), high humidity (>85%), wind-driven rain showers.

diseases.symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with characteristic concentric rings ('target board' appearance) on lower leaves first. Stem lesions cause collar rot. Sunken leathery dark lesions develop at stem end of fruits.
diseases.favorable_weather: Warm temperature (24-29°C), alternating wet and dry periods, heavy dew.

diseases.symptoms: Oval or elliptical greenish-grey water-soaked spots on leaf sheaths near waterline. Lesions enlarge and coalesce with irregular snake-skin pattern bordered by dark brown bands. Spreads upward to flag leaves.
diseases.favorable_weather: High relative humidity (85-100%), temperature 28-32°C, dense plant canopy, excessive nitrogen fertilizer.

diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked streaks starting at leaf tips and margins, expanding into wavy yellowish-white lesions that turn greyish-white. Milky bacterial ooze droplets appear on young lesions in morning. 'Kresek' phase causes seedling wilting.
diseases.favorable_weather: Temperature 25-34°C, relative humidity >70%, strong winds with continuous rains.

diseases.symptoms: Angular, pale translucent spots on lower surface of leaves covered with white powdery frosty growth resembling dusting of wheat flour (dahiya). Leaves turn yellowish brown, curl, dry and drop prematurely.
diseases.favorable_weather: Cool night temperatures (20-22°C), high humidity (>80%), cloudy weather in October-November.

diseases.pathogen_type: Fungal (Rhizoctonia bataticola & Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum)
diseases.symptoms: Sudden wilting of standing plants in patches. Taproot shows shredding of bark, dark brown vascular discoloration, and shedding of lateral fibrous roots. Plants pull out easily from soil.
diseases.favorable_weather: High soil temperatures (35-39°C), low soil moisture followed by sudden heavy irrigation, alkaline soils.

diseases.name_te: కొమ్మ ఎండు తెగులు మరియు కాయ కుళ్లు
diseases.symptoms: Circular sunken spots on ripe red fruits with black concentric rings containing fungal acervuli. Die-back begins as tender twig tips dry backwards from top to bottom, turning dirty white with black dots.
diseases.favorable_weather: Temperature 28-30°C, relative humidity >80%, intermittent rain showers after fruit setting.

diseases.symptoms: White powdery fungal patches on the lower surface of mature leaves. Upper leaf surface displays corresponding chlorotic yellow patches. Causes severe defoliation leaving bare twigs.
diseases.favorable_weather: Warm dry days (25-30°C) with cool humid nights (60-70% RH) in December-February.

diseases.pathogen_type: Viral (Chilli leaf curl virus - Begomovirus transmitted by Whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
diseases.symptoms: Upward curling and puckering of leaves, thickening of veins, shortened internodes resulting in extreme plant stunting (witches' broom effect). Drastic reduction in flowering and fruit size.
diseases.favorable_weather: Dry, hot weather favoring explosive population growth of whitefly vectors.

diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked irregular blackish-brown lesions on leaves and stems. Under humid conditions, white delicate fungal downy growth appears on underside of leaves. Fruits show large, firm, greasy brown sunken blotches.
diseases.favorable_weather: Cool temperatures (12-18°C), high relative humidity (>90%), continuous drizzle or persistent fog.

diseases.pathogen_type: Viral (Tomato leaf curl virus - Begomovirus vectored by Whitefly)
diseases.symptoms: Severe upward and inward leaf curling, interveinal chlorosis, marked reduction in leaf size, bushy stunted appearance. Flowers drop prematurely; no marketable fruit set.
diseases.favorable_weather: High temperatures (30-35°C) and low rainfall which favor heavy whitefly breeding.

diseases.symptoms: Bright yellow pustules (uredinia) arranged in narrow, parallel linear stripes along leaf veins. Upon rubbing, yellow powder adheres to fingers. Chlorosis and leaf drying follow rapidly.
diseases.favorable_weather: Cool humid weather (temperature 10-15°C), intermittent rains, morning dew in North-Western plain zone.
diseases.citation: ICAR-IIWBR Karnal Yellow Rust Surveillance Protocol 2025

diseases.symptoms: Small, round to oval, orange-brown pustules scattered randomly across leaf blades (not in stripes). Later turn black (telia) as plant approaches maturity.
diseases.favorable_weather: Moderate temperature (20-25°C) and high humidity with dew in Central and Peninsular zones.

diseases.symptoms: Only a few grains in the earhead are partially converted into black powdery teliospore mass. Diseased grains emit foul fishy odor due to trimethylamine gas.
diseases.favorable_weather: Cool cloudy weather, high humidity, light showers during wheat flowering stage (anthesis).

diseases.symptoms: Long, elliptical, spindle-shaped greyish-green to tan lesions (2.5 - 15 cm long) on leaves. Lesions merge causing extensive leaf blighting. Appears first on lower leaves and progresses upward.
diseases.favorable_weather: Moderate temperatures (18-27°C), heavy dews, relative humidity >80%.

diseases.symptoms: Small, rectangular to oval tan spots with buff to reddish-brown borders strictly confined between leaf veins. Spots coalesce causing premature foliage death.
diseases.favorable_weather: Warm temperature (20-30°C) with high relative humidity (>85%).

diseases.name_en: Tikka Leaf Spot (Early & Late Leaf Spot)
diseases.symptoms: Early spot: Circular brown lesions surrounded by prominent yellow halo. Late spot: Dark carbon-black circular spots without prominent yellow halo on lower leaf surface. Severe premature defoliation leaves naked stems.
diseases.favorable_weather: Prolonged leaf wetness, temperature 25-30°C, RH >80% for 3-4 consecutive days.

diseases.symptoms: Emerging seedlings collapse and rot at soil line. Collar region covered with profuse black sooty masses of fungal spores. Taproot decays completely.
diseases.favorable_weather: Deep sowing, high soil temperature (30-35°C), low soil moisture at seedling stage.

diseases.symptoms: Pinhead-sized grey to tan polygonal pustules (uredinia) on underside of leaves. Pustules erupt releasing brown spores; foliage yellows, desiccates and sheds prematurely.
diseases.favorable_weather: Moderate temperature (18-26°C), continuous wet weather (>6 hours dew), RH >80%.

diseases.pathogen_type: Viral (Mungbean yellow mosaic India virus vectored by Whitefly)
diseases.symptoms: Alternating bright yellow and dark green mosaic patches on young trifoliate leaves. Leaves become leathery, puckered; pods remain small with shriveled seeds.
diseases.favorable_weather: Dry periods during monsoon promoting rapid whitefly multiplication.

diseases.symptoms: Loss of turgidity, wilting and drooping of leaves starting on one side of plant. Splitting the main stem reveals a prominent dark purple-black vascular streak under the bark.
diseases.favorable_weather: Soil temperature 20-25°C, continuous cropping of pigeonpea in Vertisols.

diseases.pathogen_type: Viral (Pigeonpea sterility mosaic virus vectored by Eriophyid mite Aceria cajani)
diseases.symptoms: Bushy stunted growth, mosaic mottling of leaves, total cessation of floral bud formation (sterility). Affected plants stand out green without bearing pods.
diseases.favorable_weather: High humidity and warm conditions favoring eriophyid mite populations.

diseases.symptoms: Sudden drooping and drying of petiole and pinnae without prior yellowing. Internal vascular tissues turn dark brown to black when taproot is split vertically.
diseases.favorable_weather: Warm soil temperatures (above 25°C) at seedling and pod-filling stages, dry soil conditions.

diseases.symptoms: White or creamy porcelain-like pustules (blisters) on underside of leaves. Systemic floral infection causes hypertrophied floral malformation known as 'staghead'.
diseases.favorable_weather: Cool moist weather (temperature 12-16°C), morning fog and RH >80%.

diseases.symptoms: Concentric circular target-board spots on leaves, stems and pods (siliquae). Pod infection results in blackened shriveled seeds and premature shattering.
diseases.favorable_weather: Temperature 15-25°C with intermittent showers and overcast sky.

diseases.symptoms: Yellowing and withering of third or fourth leaf from crown. Splitting the cane longitudinally reveals crimson-red pith interspersed with characteristic white crosswise bands and alcoholic odor.
diseases.favorable_weather: Waterlogged poorly drained soils, continuous ratooning, monsoon floodwaters.

diseases.symptoms: Production of a prominent whip-like, curved, pencil-thick unbranched structure (up to 1.5m long) from apical meristem, covered with black sooty chlamydospores.
diseases.favorable_weather: Hot dry weather (30-35°C), infected setts, ratoon crops in dry soils.

diseases.symptoms: Small, sunken, water-soaked lesions that rapidly expand into large elliptical purple-centered spots with yellow halo on leaves and seed stalks. Stalks break at the lesion.
diseases.favorable_weather: Warm temperature (25-30°C), relative humidity >85%, heavy thrips feeding punctures.

diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaf margins turning black necrotic; white mildew growth on underside in morning. Tubers develop dry, rusty brown subterranean rot extending into flesh.
diseases.favorable_weather: Temperature 10-20°C, RH >90%, persistent dense fog or drizzling rainfall.
diseases.citation: ICAR-CPRI Shimla Late Blight Forecasting System 2025

diseases.symptoms: Progressive yellowing of lower leaves from margins inwards. Pseudostem collar becomes soft and water-soaked, detaching easily with slight pull. Rhizomes rot into foul soft watery mass.
diseases.favorable_weather: Water stagnation, heavy soils with poor drainage, temperature 25-30°C during monsoon.

diseases.symptoms: Oblong to circular brown spots with grey center and dark brown margin appearing on both leaf surfaces. In advanced stages, spots coalesce drying out entire leaf lamina.
diseases.favorable_weather: High humidity (80-90%), cloudy days, intermittent rains in August-October.
